sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2011. A Phula comparative lexicon: Phola, Phuza, Muji, Phowa, Azha. SIL Language and Culture Documentation and Description 18. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.note: Section 3.3 'Southern Muji phonology in brief' (pp. 8-9) describes the syllable template, segments and five tones of SOUTHERN Muji (PJZ datapoint) with tone-sandhi notes; the word 'stress' does not occur anywhere in the 536 kB text. Northern Muji (datapoint XPC, Xiepo, Shuitian, Mengzi; p. 4) is not sketched and is mentioned only once in the phonology section: 'Ngwi-branch prenasalization has almost completely merged with plain voicing in Northern and Southern Muji alike' (p. 8). No stress statement for any Muji variety.
sources.venue: SIL Language and Culture Documentation and Description

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-120: split [ymj] into [ymc] Southern Muji, [ymx] Northern Muji, [ymq] Qila Muji, [ymi] Moji, [ymz] Muzi (adopted 2008-01-14). SIL International.
sources.note: Intelligibility scores (Northern Muji speakers scored.60 on a Southern Muji recorded text test) and identity rationale from Pelkey's 2005-2006 survey; nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin. 2005. Puzzling over Phula: toward the synthesis and statement of a sub-branch. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 28(2): 43-78. doi:10.32655/ltba.28.2.02
sources.note: Classification/ethnonym survey of the Phula cluster; Muji appears only in lexical-similarity and classification discussion (the scanned text). No phonology, no stress.

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2006. Muji uncorked: A first tasting of the dialects, distinctives and distribution. Paper presented at the 39th International Conference on Sino-Tibetan Languages and Linguistics (ICSTLL 39), University of Washington, Seattle, 15-17 September 2006. [1-page abstract archived from depts.washington.edu/icstll39/abstracts/; full paper unpublished, not located]
sources.note: Conference abstract: says the Muji dialects share a redistribution of the Proto-Ngwi tonal split reflecting an earlier tone merger; no tone inventory or analysis for Northern Muji is given.

tone.quote: Following these sections, Muji is defined linguistically according to phonological, morphological and lexical innovations apparent in affiliated dialects. Notably, such innovations include a correlative redistribution of the *Ngwi tonal split that points back to a intermediate merger, the re-introduction of nasal finals—a rare feature in the syllable templates of modern-day Ngwi groups beyond Southern Ngwi (Hani-Akha)—and a unique diminutive …

Ch. 5 'Phula phonologies: Five representative sketches' (pp. 223-270) and Ch. 6 'The language clades of Phula Proper' (pp. 271-351), where Northern Muji (XPC) tone and segment data appear.
